sections.title: 6.1 Passports of existing models
sections.content: The nearest direction of research is comparative study of the behavior of language models under load on the widest possible sample of models of different classes and manufacturers. The main interest lies not only in the quantitative estimates of the instruction capacity, but also in the regularities of the degradation of the quality of instruction execution: the composition of the significant load factors, the character of their action and the mathematical form of the corresponding dependencies. The instruction capacity is only one of the characteristics derived from these laws, whereas the laws themselves give fuller description of the behavior of model under load. There are no grounds to assume that the regularities established for GPT-4o mini are universal. Larger models or models of other architectures may show qualitatively different dependencies: the appearance of extrema instead of monotonic change, the replacement of linear dependence on the logarithm of the load by power one, or change of the very set of significant axes. systematic comparison of such regularities across different models and their generations will make it possible to study the possible connection between the character of the degradation and the features of the internal structure of the models. Thus catalog of passports has double value: as an experimental basis of comparative study of language models and as tool for the quantitative evaluation of their capabilities. The proposed methodology provides the flexibility needed for such studies: the composition of the load axes and the form of the dependencies are determined from experimental data rather than set priori (Sections 4 and 5.2). The main practical limitations in building the catalog remain the availability of tokenizers and the cost of measurements. Access to tokenizers. replacement remains an atomic operation only if both words of the rule are encoded by one token of the tokenizer of the measured model (Section 3.2). common vocabulary for all models is not needed: the single-token property is required only for the tokenizer of the model under study, and if the vocabulary of each model is selected by the same rules, the comparability of measurements is ensured by averaging over random sets of words and rules. sections.title: 6.2 Measuring prompts
sections.content: Prompts have become the main means of programming the behavior of language models. Their development, complication and optimization have acquired the character of an independent engineering activity, yet there is still no generally accepted quantitative measure of the instruction load 2https://www.morphllm.com/llm-api, https://mem0.ai/library/llms-and-models/openai-api-pricing, 25.10.2026. 63 they create. The present work proposes to consider prompt as an object of metrological measurement and to express its weight in equivalents of elementary instructionsreplacement rules. The goal of such measurement is not to evaluate the quality of the prompt itself or the success of the task set in it, but to determine the magnitude of the instruction load that it creates for language model. The literature review (Section 2) did not reveal studies in which the load of arbitrary prompts was measured in common comparable units. The closest to this formulation is the observation that the quality of instruction execution decreases when parallel task is added [28], but the cited work does not introduce quantitative measure of this effect. The instruction weight of prompt differs fundamentally from its formal characteristicsthe length of the text and the number of instructions it contains. Many simple independent requirements may create smaller load than few complex interrelated conditions. Therefore counting instructions or tokens does not by itself make it possible to evaluate the demands of prompt on the capabilities of language model. The proposed measurement aims to determine its actual instruction load, expressed on the common scale of elementary replacement rules. The proposed method of weighing prompts is based on an indirect measurement of the instruction load. Instead of evaluating the success of executing the prompt under study, one measures its effect on the quality of executing an independent control task with reference answer known in advance and calibrated dependence on the load. The word replacement test serves as such task. The prompt under study is added to the task of the instrument next to the table of rules, after which the decrease of the share of right replacements is measured. The laws of the passport of the model make it possible to express the corresponding change of the logit through an equivalent number of additional replacement rules, which defines the instruction weight of the prompt. The fundamental advantage of the method lies in the possibility of measuring the load of arbitrary prompts without developing special tests to evaluate the quality of executing the tasks they contain. The conversion into equivalents of rules rests on the assumption that the additional load of prompt acts on the logit of right replacement in the same way as an increase of the number of rules. The validity of this representation is yet to be established experimentally. The instruction capacity of model and the weight of prompt, expressed in the same units, form common scale for comparing the capabilities of model and the demands of the task set before it. This will make it possible to evaluate quantitatively not only the ability of model to execute instructions, but also the load created by specific prompt, the available reserve of capacity and its change when the prompt is optimized. Thereby the proposed approach opens the possibility of passing from the experimental study of the limitations of language models to quantitative methods of designing applied systems based on them. In this formulation the passport of model is not only an independent result of the study, but also necessary calibration basis of the future prompt meter. It is the established laws of the dependence of the quality of instruction execution on the load that make it possible to convert the decrease of the results of the control task into an equivalent number of rules. full measurement of model (Section 6.1) requires significant costs, but after the calibration each subsequent weighing is expected to be carried out using the known laws, spending only small fraction of the resources needed for the initial measurement. Thus the developed methodology creates the prerequisites not only for systematic study of the instruction capacity of language models, but also for creating new class of measuring instruments intended for the quantitative evaluation of the load of applied prompts.

sections.title: 7 Conclusion
sections.content: This work proposes way to measure the behavior of language model under controlled instruction load and builds an instrument that implements it. The load is formed by rules replacing singletoken words in text without meaning: such an instruction is atomic, the rules are independent by the construction of the task, and the outcome of each application of rule is determined by computable reference answer without an evaluator (Section 3). One rule serves as conventional unit of load, and every occurrence of word to be replaced becomes Bernoulli trial with known position in the answer and known rule number. The statistical model describes the logit of right replacement by the sum of the contributions of the load axes and the shift of the request, and contains no common level that depends on the choice of reference bins. The form of each contribution is first measured by bins without assumptions and then described by smooth law, and the approximation shift correction restores reference level that does not depend on the coding (Section 4). The instruction capacity is defined as the solution of an inverse problemthe load at which the share of right replacements falls to given level of qualityand is expressed in rules with an uncertainty. The measurement of GPT-4o mini showed that the form measured by bins without assumptions is regular for each load factor and is described by law with small number of parameters (Section 5). The text length and the word position act not as sum of independent losses, but as two interacting constraints: the length sets the level of quality at the beginning of the answer, and the word position sets the regularity of its subsequent decrease, common to all lengths. The replacement density acts as an independent saturating factor, and the size of the rule list and the position of rule in it act as two different factors from which the price of each next rule is composed. The collapse of the answer obeys its own laws: it is determined by the load of the text and the progress through the answer, not by the number of instructions held. From these laws the instruction, fatigue and guaranteed instruction capacities of the model are computed (Section 5.5), and every number of the passport is recomputed from the published points (Section 8). The laws found for GPT-4o mini describe one model, and the nearest task is to build the passports of many models and to compare the very laws of their behavior (Section 6.1). The ultimate goal of the instrument is the weighing of prompts: the passport of model serves as the calibration of meter that expresses the instruction load of an arbitrary prompt in the same units as the capacity of the model (Section 6.2).

sections.title: 8 Code and data availability
sections.content: The public part of the instrument is published in an open repository https://github. com/kutomanovhennadii/instruction-capacity. It contains the code that executes one pointgenerating task from three seeds, calling the model and validating the answerthe code that builds the passport and checks it, the vocabulary together with the code that produced it, the documents of the method and the published measurement of GPT-4o mini: the records of all points with prompts, answers and token counters, the description of the measurement with the checksums of the files, and the passport.

sections.title: Any number of the passport given in the article is recomputed from the published points by
sections.content: the command python scripts/build_passport.py artefacts/pilot_gpt4o_mini_v34 --out-dir my_passport and the integrity and reproducibility of the published measurement are checked by the command 65 python scripts/verify.py artefacts/pilot_gpt4o_mini_v The check compares the checksums of the files, compares the vocabulary with its reference version, regenerates the rule list and the text of each request from its seeds and recomputes the passport, comparing it with the published one within the precision of the computations; it does not call the language model. With the same code one can measure points on another model and build its passport. The points of the published measurement were chosen by an adaptive planning technology developed by the author: it decides which points to measure from the results of the points already measured. This technology forms the closed part of the instrument and is not disclosed: neither its design nor its rules for choosing points are published. The passport does not depend on it: it is computed from the published points alone, whoever chose them, and therefore every number of the passport can be checked without the closed part. sections.content: The published request at the point (D, n, m) = (4, 5, 2), used as an example in Section 3.3, is given below in full: text of 20 words and two rules, the order seed is zero, and the lines of the rules follow in the order of the choice.
